item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-08
item.description:
• Context compression is following two routes. One rewrites reasoning history into compact state records (Reasoning History Compaction, 👍13). The other compresses tool outputs into latent tokens (Coca-Cola, tokens down 70.01%–89.24%).
  • Switching between tasks is now a measurable failure point for context management. Switch-SWE found that interleaving unfinished tasks cut the solve rate of 7 coding agents by 11.5 points on average. A context-management plugin recovered 5.5–15.5 points.
  • Continually evolving harnesses forget. Meta-Harness dropped from 94.0% to 32.0% on SWE-Bench (see section 2).
  • Guardrails are the most crowded theme among the other Agent papers: Caper and LeanGuard both intercept tool calls before they execute.
  • Cognitive Symbionts went from 40 to 114 upvotes. It is still a vision paper with no experiments (see the 11-07 report).

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-07
item.description:
• Harnesses are the most concentrated topic today. Harness-S (ranked first), the continual-evolution forgetting study, RoboArchitect and TinyAstral all work on evolving or transferring an agent's harness (the scaffolding around the model).
  • Continual evolution forgets, with numbers: Meta-Harness on SWE-Bench fell from 94.0% to 32.0%, a 66% relative drop.
  • Context management now has measurable gains. Switch-SWE's task-switching plugin improves OpenCode by 5.5–15.5 percentage points, and rewriting reasoning history can cut agent cost.
  • KV cache shows up in two directions. SwarmEvolve has agents communicate through it, and the SIMPLE law measures cached agentic requests at 4.8x the energy of ordinary ones.
  • The position paper Cognitive Symbionts has the most upvotes in the context/memory group (👍40), but it is a vision paper with no experiments.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-06
item.description:
• Context management is moving from compressing text to passing KV state in latent space. Octopus (a DAG of forked KV states), SwarmEvolve (agents pass KV cache to each other) and CacheGraft (documents pre-encoded as KV) all appeared on the same day, in the New section.
  • The harness is now an optimization target. Harness-S (👍51 in New, the day's highest), ParetoSaddler and RoboArchitect all improve or evolve harnesses automatically.
  • Memory work is getting deeper. EvoMemState turns memory from independent facts into facts with relational state, and MemSteer generates supervision from user histories to tune memory design.
  • Long-horizon context problems now have a direct benchmark. Switch-SWE tests whether an agent recovers after switching tasks, and its context-management plugin adds 5.5 to 15.5 percentage points.
  • Many benchmark papers (FrontierPhysics, MCPHallu and others) conclude that frontier agents still have clear gaps.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-05
item.description:
• The top paper on the hot list is Route Anything (👍82). It studies model and policy routing, not context engineering.
  • Context papers cluster on two threads, automatic harness optimization and automatic memory optimization: ParetoSaddler (👍16), MemSteer (👍8), GEPA-Curator (👍8) and RoboArchitect (👍8).
  • Switch-SWE measures how much coding agents lose when switching tasks (11.5 points on average) and offers a context-management plugin.
  • Last night's new papers include five on context compression: SpecCompact, SumOne, Coca-Cola, Visual Token Routing and reasoning-history compression.
  • Continual harness evolution now has evidence of forgetting: with Meta-Harness, SWE-Bench accuracy fell from 94.0% to 32.0% (paper).

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-04
item.description:
• The most-liked papers are a survey and a harness paper. Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics leads with 👍127. CoworkOS has 👍96 and 104 stars on its code.
  • Several empirical studies look at memory and context management: what happens after a task switch (Switch-SWE), what a compressed memory should keep (Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong), and when memory helps at all (What Is This Memory Useful For?, in the New section).
  • Two papers keep history or output outside the agent's context. SWE-Trail uses history only to steer data collection. GeoFaham (New) stores full outputs outside the context and passes only identifiers and summaries.
  • Harnesses are now a research subject: verification strategy (Rethinking Verification), automatic harness evolution (RoboArchitect, ParetoSaddler, EvoGroup), and how skills evolve on GitHub (84,200 skills).
  • Computer-use agent (CUA) training loops cluster on the list. CUA-Master scores 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, and NorthCUA appears in the same window.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-03
item.description:
• "Harness" (the scaffolding around a model: prompts, tools, verification, memory) dominates both the hot and new lists. Topics include how to design verification, how much a trained policy depends on its harness, automatic harness evolution, and whether continually evolving a harness causes forgetting.
  • Memory and compression research is asking whether the right things were kept. Rules that survive context compression are still violated, and both "relevant" and "rare" filters for memory summaries fail.
  • Skill self-optimization keeps rising: Skill^∞, R²Orch, and in the new list Zep Agent Skills, all about generating, refining and retiring skills.
  • Inference-serving papers now treat long agent contexts as their own workload: prefix caching, KV cache collapse, scheduling.
  • The two highest-scoring papers from last night are CoworkOS (👍85) and CUA-Master (👍90). Both ship code, with 40+ stars each.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context Papers · 2026-11-04
item.description:
• The hot list clusters around harnesses and the interfaces between model and environment. Three papers (verification strategy, MCP vs. CLI, policy-harness coupling) ask how much a model keeps when the harness changes.
  • Two results on compressing memory and experience point the same way. ReGE merges multiple run logs into one piece of guidance and cuts construction tokens by 95–98%. CrossProfile shows that what a memory keeps matters more than the selection strategy, and a full transcript did worse than taking no notes.
  • Two papers kept climbing: TAO (👍 15→95), tool-aware agent scheduling with cache reuse, and WorkFactory (👍 30→58), occupational task synthesis.
  • Many of the new papers are about context management: soft-token compression (ASTC), vector-free memory retrieval (KITE), knowledge compilation (RAGFlow), subquadratic sparse attention (LSA, ZHA) and retrieval completeness for multi-tool requests.
  • Benchmarks are moving toward process: checking for skipped required steps (TauIndianBankBench), investment research on a frozen information set (ILE), verifier reuse (AgentProofBench).

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-11-01
item.description:
• Harnesses and skill/experience reuse lead the chart: HaMo (👍21, +16 in 4 days), Δτ-Bench (👍24), ReGE and Skill^∞.
  • The harness itself is now a research subject. 2610.34577 compares 17 verification designs and finds an independent critic review is the best value. 2610.37255 shows that swapping the harness sharply degrades an already-trained policy.
  • Benchmarks dominate the non-context agent papers, and they agree that finishing a task is not the same as satisfying the user (RealCLI, PersonaCUABench, Co-Design Bench).
  • Smarter memory compression is not always better: 2610.37624 finds that full transcripts give lower accuracy than taking no notes at all.

• Reverse-engineering agents still top the chart: morluto/rea has 414,491 stars and +3,525/day, 27 days above the threshold, with a 7-day average of 5,628. Its one-day peak was 54,068 on 10-12, and it is now cooling. A defense aimed at it, qybaihe/bla (1,652 stars, +400/day), appeared the same day.
  • Cost control has a big-company entry: microsoft/TokenEconomizer 🆕 has 2,712 stars and +1,368/day, after +205 → +378 → +1,515 over three days.
  • Phone and desktop computer-use agents broke out together: wangzan101/Mika 🆕 at +1,840/day, and vercel-labs/agent-desktop at +1,755/day (it got only 1–4 stars a day for the previous 13 days).
  • The long-term memory layer thedotmack/claude-mem jumped from about +300/day to +977 (10-29) and +1,639 (10-30), and is at +1,619/day today.
  • "Anti-AI-slop" and design-taste skills remain the strongest Skills category: pbakaus/impeccable is on a 39-day streak, and Nutlope/hallmark averages 1,701/day over 7 days.

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-31
item.description:
• morluto/rea (reverse engineering with agents) is still #1 at ≈+3,525/day, down again from +4,720 on 10-30. It has been on the list at least 6 days running since 10-26 (see the 10-30 report).
  • Its 7 YouTube videos total ▶1,314,906 views, and a 10-10 HN post drew 814 points and 340 comments.
  • The contrast worth noting today: wangzan101/Mika, an Android phone agent, gained +1,840/day almost entirely from the author's own posts plus one large account's repost. The author says it hit 400 stars less than 24 hours after going open source. vercel-labs/agent-desktop, which drives desktop computer use through the accessibility tree, gained +1,755/day with almost no promotion on X.
  • Cost and privacy are running in parallel. microsoft/TokenEconomizer claims it cuts coding-agent cost by about 18–31% on SWE-Bench. claude-mem reached HN over issue #5176, where the issue's author says installation uploads prompts.
  • The top HN story today is the Prospero coding harness (90 points / 60 comments). The same day, Tom's Hardware reported that Claude has started blocking game-cloning and reverse-engineering requests (HN: 20 points).

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-10-31
item.description:
• Harness and skill self-evolution is the busiest theme. 2610.33024 finds the same skill helps strong models and hurts weak ones. 2610.35434 optimizes skills recursively. 2610.34724 and 2610.33861 distill trajectories into retrievable experience.
  • Prompt cache is now showing up in agent engineering. 2610.34241 measures about 69.4 s to first token for cold-prefix requests versus about 2.8 s for high-reuse ones. 2610.37230 puts cache reuse and tool-return timing into scheduling.
  • The hottest paper is Youtu-Parsing-Omni, with HF 👍152 and +132 in one day. It is a multimodal parsing (perception) layer for agents.
  • Several evaluations agree that a bigger reasoning budget doesn't mean better results. 2610.34491 finds the highest effort setting costs up to 42x the lowest and isn't necessarily more accurate.
  • "A simple harness beats a complex one" shows up repeatedly: RoboHarness, h1.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-10-30
item.description:
• Two threads dominate the hot list. One is keeping skills and tools current as the environment changes (Δτ-Bench, Skill Adaptation). The other is faster inference and caching for long-horizon agents (DLite, FlatCake).
  • Last night's new papers are heavy on memory and context: CORAL's context reset, memory optimization in MemSteer and MUSE, and context compaction for world models.
  • Harness self-evolution keeps drawing attention. Self-Evolving Agent Harness has 387 GitHub stars, Skill Adaptation gained 21 upvotes in 3 days, and SkillCompiler and the Skill utility shifts paper work on the same problem.
  • Security research is reaching skills: one paper scans 1.53 million skills, and another covers skill scanners.
  • Three projects stand out on GitHub: InternLM/Intern-Decision (775 stars), Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA (441) and zgcagi/Harness-RSI (387).

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-30
item.description:
• morluto/rea still tops the growth list at ⭐410,966 and +4,720/day. It has charted for at least 5 straight days since 10-26, with daily growth easing (+6,962 → +6,095 → +5,248 → +5,348 → +4,720; see the 10-26 through 10-29 reports).
  • REA's exposure comes from two channels: list and promo posts with 👁491,616, and 7 YouTube videos with ▶1,105,082 views combined.
  • The biggest security story is on HN: version 2.1.313 of the official Claude Code VS Code extension was backdoored on the Cursor marketplace. Three related threads scored 641, 393 and 235. The same day, an issue on thedotmack/claude-mem (#5176) accused it of uploading prompts at install time.
  • "Free, no key" projects spread through user tutorials. Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model has 28 organic posts from 27 accounts and 👁326,683. The tutorial copy is near-identical, and the repo has an unverified "legal letter" dispute.
  • Big exposure, little real discussion: cloudflare/security-audit-skill (influencer 👁312,476 vs organic 👁10,733) and milind-soni/OpenMausBot (the author's own single post is 98% of its media exposure).
  • Token cost and memory dominate organic talk: the "memory tax" paper, the AgentBaton paper, and a measurement showing cache dominates spend.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-30
item.description:
• morluto/rea is still #1 at 410,966 ⭐ and +4,720/day, 26 days into its run. Daily gains have fallen from 17,573 to 5,147 over 14 days (7-day average 5,941, 28-day average 14,595, 30-week peak +54,078 on Oct 12). It has spawned a ring of derivatives: qybaihe/bla, a defense against REA-style reverse-engineering agents, is 5 days old and at +883/day, and two rea-topic awesome lists keep growing.
  • The DeepSeek Harness ("dsh") plugin ecosystem keeps expanding. deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness has 266,563 ⭐ and +949/day, with its 7-day average at or above 666 for 19 straight days. Many projects carry the dsh-plugin topic: free-model access, a desktop app, a knowledge base, a chart skill.
  • Design "anti-slop" skills are accelerating. pbakaus/impeccable is at +1,971/day, 39 days running, and its daily gain rose from 392 to 2,462 over 14 days.
  • Long-term memory and token-cost tools both popped up today. thedotmack/claude-mem hit +1,278/day after roughly 200–340/day before. microsoft/TokenEconomizer is 17 days old and at +853/day.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-29
item.description:
• Reverse engineering has become a cluster. morluto/rea has 406,246 stars and +5,348/day, 25 straight days of high growth, with a 7-day average of 6,385. Several awesome lists have appeared around it, plus a counter-project, qybaihe/bla.
  • "Anti-AI-look" design skills are the hottest skill category. pbakaus/impeccable is at +2,787/day, with a 7-day average of 1,295 against a 28-day average of 742, so it is accelerating. Nutlope/hallmark is at +1,490/day and Leonxlnx/taste-skill at +1,074/day.
  • Large companies are publishing skill and methodology repos. Google, Cloudflare, NVIDIA, Microsoft, MiniMax and JetBrains all appear on today's list.
  • The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin ecosystem is growing. deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness has 265,614 stars and +1,029/day, and many repos on the list carry the dsh-plugin tag.
  • vectorize-io/hindsight, a long-term memory layer, is at +1,429/day, the highest among memory projects.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-10-29
item.description:
• Memory Tax is the most talked-about context paper today. It reports that many dedicated memory systems do worse than naive RAG in a good number of cases, so their net value is negative.
  • The Trinity (👍543, 1 day on the list, +236) tops the hot list. It treats the harness as something that evolves recursively and routes tasks by capability.
  • Harness self-evolution and scaling is a cluster: The Trinity, HarnessPro, Harness Scaling, SERA and Self-Evolving Harness (see the 10-25 report).
  • Memory benchmarks keep showing that having memory is not the same as using it well. The best method on HABIT-Bench reaches only 33.61% macro-average accuracy.
  • Long-horizon RL is assigning credit at the turn level: MPO (👍379, 1 day on the list, +328).

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-29
item.description:
• morluto/rea is still first at +5,348/day (⭐406,246). Its exposure comes from long "Opus 5.5 + REA can reverse anything" posts and YouTube tutorials (one at ▶499,129). Influencer exposure totals 👁491,596. Organic discussion shows 👁441,063, but most of that is an unrelated tweet.
  • Design skills crowd the list: pbakaus/impeccable +2,787/day, Nutlope/hallmark +1,490/day, Leonxlnx/taste-skill +1,074/day. All sell "make AI-built pages not look like AI". Organic discussion is thin, and the rankings lean on list posts and GitHub Trending bot reposts.
  • Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model (a free-model plugin for DeepSeek Harness) is at +2,029/day, driven almost entirely by "freebie" tutorial tweets from 16 real accounts (👁293,320). A "legal letter" posted in issue #576 is being questioned by the community.
  • google/elephant-goldfish-model has 5,541 ⭐ and +1,313/day, with growth that looks organic. One Chinese-language explainer from @awe0_io got ❤1,040 👁53,668, and one YouTube video reached ▶166,990.
  • Topics: whether agent memory beats naive RAG (the Memory Tax paper), coding-agent security and privacy (AGENTS.md hijacking, a Claude Code privacy dispute on HN), and parallel multi-agent tools (Orca, ThinkRail, SuperPlane).

item.title: Agent Community Buzz & Growth Attribution · 2026-10-28
item.description:
• morluto/rea has ⭐400,898 and +5,248/day. It has charted 6 days in a row (10-23 to 10-28, see the 10-23 to 10-27 reports). Its exposure comes from about 1.11M YouTube views plus promotional-sounding X long posts. Real usage feedback is thin.
  • Free models and model routing are climbing: Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model at +2,067/day and yetone/magpie at +1,010/day. The first is a third-party plugin tied to a publicly posted "lawyer's letter" incident.
  • Two "anti-AI-look design skills" charted together: Nutlope/hallmark at +1,912/day and pbakaus/impeccable at +1,471/day. The first has real recommendations from big accounts. The second spreads almost entirely through list posts.
  • "Write the spec first, then have an amnesiac AI review it" is a new theme with big-company backing. google/elephant-goldfish-model is at +1,594/day (first appearance today). cloudflare/security-audit-skill (independent verifiers) and JetBrains/thinkrail (Living Specs) point the same way.
  • No tweets posted today made it into the data, so the new-signal section draws on topic tweets from one day ago.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-28
item.description:
• Skills drove most of today's growth, in three flavors at once: design (Nutlope/hallmark, +1,912/day), methodology (obra/superpowers, +1,025/day) and Google's google/elephant-goldfish-model (+1,594/day, ⭐4,228).

  • HKUDS/DeepTutor jumped to +2,228/day (⭐47,537) after 60–300 a day earlier, with 1,478 → 2,254 over the last two days. gitroomhq/postiz-app and nightly-labs/openbot show the same two-day takeoff.
  • The dsh ecosystem is growing. deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness is at +1,100/day (⭐264,585), and its plugin Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model is at +2,067/day, 24 days running.
  • cloudflare/security-audit-skill has grown steadily for 44 days, at +1,548/day.

item.title: Agent Papers · 2026-10-28
item.description:
• Memory research is swinging back to raw retrieval. Raw-RAG says naive RAG ranks first in 6 of 7 settings. Tonight's new Memory Tax reaches the same conclusion: complex memory systems often lose to naive RAG.
  • The harness is now a research subject. TraceTrial-Bench benchmarks harness reliability itself (👍291, +128 in one day). Self-Evolving Agent Harness, HarnessPro, Harness Scaling, The Trinity and Rethinking Verification cover how harnesses evolve, get trained and get verified.
  • Context gets lost inside harness pipelines. Context Is a Pipeline, Not a Window found that 3,827 of 11,189 tool results were truncated before reaching the model across 720 runs.
  • Training data quality for tool use: Trajectory2Gym lifts the three-benchmark average by 16.9–29.8 points across 5 Qwen3 sizes (👍359).
  • GUI and computer-use agents keep heating up. FocusGUI went from 31 to 230 likes. OpenGCUA has 441 GitHub stars.

item.title: Agent & Agent Context on GitHub · 2026-10-27
item.description:
• Reverse engineering is the hottest topic today. morluto/rea gained +6,095/day to reach 395,650 stars, on a 23-day run of high growth. Four awesome-lists on the same theme are also climbing.
  • The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) ecosystem keeps growing. deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness has 263,485 stars (+1,117/day). The dsh plugin Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model is at +1,971/day, 23 days running.
  • Skills are the main way agent capabilities get distributed. A design skill (Nutlope/hallmark, +2,822/day), a security skill (cloudflare/security-audit-skill, 43 days running) and a methodology skill (google/elephant-goldfish-model, +1,110/day) are all rising at once.
  • Multi-agent "control panel" projects keep attracting stars: stablyai/orca (126 days running), herdrdev/herdr (130 days, by the 7-day-average measure), and newcomers JetBrains/thinkrail (+1,227 in a day) and nightly-labs/openbot (+840).
  • Long-term memory and security scanning for skills are both heating up: NVIDIA/SkillSpector is at +815/day, and akitaonrails/ai-memory is 14 days running.

item.title: Agent 社区热议 & 增长归因 · 2026-10-27
item.description:
• Fastest grower is still morluto/rea: ⭐395,650, +6,095/day. Organic discussion jumped on X posts claiming Anthropic restricted REA inside Claude (users' claim; nothing in the data confirms it officially).
  • Anti-"AI look" design skills are a trend: Nutlope/hallmark at +2,822/day, and the community project elayadesign/ai-design-skills drew ❤10,173 👁645,417 on a single tweet.
  • Splitting the finder from the verifier travels best: cloudflare/security-audit-skill got 👁594,554 from one organic recommendation by @jurbed.
  • Multi-harness and multi-model layers are heating up: makecindy/cindy (swaps Claude Code and Codex), yetone/magpie, the deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness plugin ecosystem, stablyai/orca, HarnessRouter, plus "self-improving harness" talk (Octopus OS, Harness²).
  • Exposure and organic discussion are badly mismatched: Panniantong/Agent-Reach, affaan-m/ECC and the Claude Opus video-list repos get reach from listicles and big accounts with little real discussion. JetBrains/thinkrail grew mostly on Hacker News (239 points).

item.title: Agent Weekly · 2026-W43 (2026-10-19 ~ 2026-10-25)
item.description:
• morluto/rea stays #1 with ⭐382,593 and +88,243 this week (Trending's weekly figure), about +5.5k/day over the 4 days. Claims on X that Anthropic added reverse-engineering restrictions to Claude drove heavy organic discussion, but they are user retellings with no official confirmation.
  • cloudflare/security-audit-skill is the cleanest organic growth: +12,680 this week, daily gains rising (+2,979 → +2,038 → +2,177 → +2,744), near-zero influencer exposure, 👁1,027,652 of organic discussion.
  • Multi-agent orchestration and harnesses became a category: Orca +9,828 this week, the dsh plugin ecosystem around DeepSeek Harness, HarnessRouter letting a Grok bot dispatch to other vendors' harnesses, and Google's Harness² all appeared together.
  • Retrieval and memory projects are diverging. xerj has +8,080 this week but its daily gain fell from +1,180 to +255, while graphify holds at +573 to +632/day. The Raw-RAG paper argues plain RAG beats complex memory systems, which puts pressure on this group.
  • "Free model" projects and Opus 5.5 video repos grew on distribution, with risks. dsh-our-free-model has ≈+7,286 this week amid privacy and compliance questions. lemo-opuscar and similar repos drew 👁750,397 of influencer exposure with far less real usage feedback.
